note: depth pass 4: L4 例词补充

words.glossEn: the official power to make legal decisions
words.etymology: 拉丁 jurisdictio < jus/juris「法」+ dicere（宣告）
derivation: jur（法）+ -is- + dic（宣告）+ -tion → 依法宣告的权力
words.example: The case falls outside this court's jurisdiction.

words.glossEn: a group of citizens who decide a case in court
words.etymology: 古法语 juree < 拉丁 jurare「宣誓」< jus「法」
derivation: jur（法、宣誓）+ -y → 宣誓断案的一群人
words.example: The jury returned a verdict after two hours.

words.glossEn: a unit of mass equal to one thousand grams
words.etymology: 希腊 khilioi「一千」+ gramma「小重量」
derivation: kilo（千）+ gram（克）→ 一千克
words.example: The bag weighs just over one kilogram.

words.glossEn: a unit of length equal to one thousand meters
words.etymology: 希腊 khilioi「一千」+ metron「尺度」
derivation: kilo（千）+ metr（度量）+ -er → 一千米
words.example: The village lies a kilometer from the main road.

words.glossEn: the secretion of milk; the period of suckling
words.etymology: 拉丁 lactatio < lactare「分泌乳汁」< lac/lactis「乳」
derivation: lact（乳）+ -ation → 产乳的过程
words.example: The mother returned to work after lactation ended.

words.glossEn: the sugar found in milk
words.etymology: 拉丁 lac/lactis「乳」+ 化学后缀 -ose（糖）
derivation: lact（乳）+ -ose（糖）→ 乳中的糖
words.example: He avoids milk because of lactose intolerance.

words.glossEn: a thing used for tying; letters joined in print
words.etymology: 拉丁 ligatura < ligare「捆绑」
derivation: lig（绑）+ -at- + -ure → 用于绑的东西
words.example: The surgeon closed the vessel with a ligature.

words.glossEn: a system of faith and worship
words.etymology: 拉丁 religio，常释为 re-（再）+ ligare（绑）「重新系紧」
derivation: re（再、回）+ lig（绑）+ -ion → 把人重新系住的约束
words.example: The two communities practise the same religion.

words.glossEn: the ability to read and write
words.etymology: 拉丁 littera「字母」+ -acy
derivation: liter（字母）+ -acy（能力、状态）→ 识字母的能力
words.example: Adult literacy rose sharply in one generation.

words.glossEn: relating to literature or formal writing
words.etymology: 拉丁 litterarius < littera「字母」
derivation: liter（字母、文字）+ -ary → 与文字作品有关的
words.example: The novel won a major literary prize.

words.glossEn: a large single block of stone
words.etymology: 希腊 monos「单一」+ lithos「石」
derivation: mono（单一）+ lith（石）→ 一整块石头
words.example: A weathered monolith stands at the centre of the ring.

words.glossEn: printing from a flat stone or metal plate
words.etymology: 希腊 lithos「石」+ graphein「写、刻」
derivation: lith（石）+ o + graph（刻写）+ -y → 在石版上刻写印刷
words.example: The poster was produced by stone lithography.

words.glossEn: clear and easy to understand; bright
words.etymology: 拉丁 lucidus < lucere「发光」
derivation: luc（光）+ -id → 有光的 → 明白的
words.example: She gave a lucid account of the experiment.

words.glossEn: giving off light; bright
words.etymology: 拉丁 luminosus < lumen/luminis「光」
derivation: lumin（光）+ -ous（充满）→ 充满光的
words.example: The dial is painted with a luminous compound.

words.glossEn: impressively large or beautiful
words.etymology: 拉丁 magnificus < magnus「大」+ facere「做」
derivation: magn（大）+ -ific（做）+ -ent → 做得很大 → 宏伟
words.example: The hall opened onto a magnificent view of the valley.

words.glossEn: to make something appear larger
words.etymology: 拉丁 magnificare < magnus「大」+ facere「做」
derivation: magn（大）+ -ify（使…）→ 使变大
words.example: The lens can magnify the image ten times.

words.glossEn: a cone used to make the voice carry
words.etymology: 希腊 megas「大」+ phōnē「声音」
derivation: mega（大）+ phone（声音）→ 放大声音的器具
words.example: The marshal shouted through a megaphone.

words.glossEn: a very large prehistoric stone
words.etymology: 希腊 megas「大」+ lithos「石」
derivation: mega（大）+ lith（石）→ 巨石
words.example: The tomb is built from megaliths weighing several tons.

words.glossEn: the chemical processes that sustain life
words.etymology: 希腊 metabolē「改变」< meta-（转变）+ ballein（投掷）
derivation: meta（转变）+ bol（投）+ -ism → 体内不断转换的过程
words.example: Regular exercise raises your resting metabolism.

words.glossEn: a figure of speech applying one thing's name to another
words.etymology: 希腊 metaphora「转移」< meta-（越过）+ pherein（携带）
derivation: meta（越过）+ phor（携带）→ 把意义搬过去
words.example: 'A sea of troubles' is a metaphor.
